subject: Throughput chokepoint impacting ClearBrooke — exec approval needed
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@clearbrooke.ai>
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 22:12:00 -0000
Subject: Sudden throughput collapse on our production traffic (charts attached)

Diego —

We started seeing a sharp drop in successful responses around 14:05 PST today. Traffic volume is the same but latencies spiked and a lot of requests returned 429 / transient internal errors. Our engineers captured traces and request ids and I attached a high-level chart showing TPS vs successful token consumption. This began right after a scheduled promotion of a new multi-tenant rollout on our side.

We are in the middle of a live demo to a major client and this is causing timeouts and degraded quality. Can Redwood confirm whether this is a capacity issue, a quota hit, or some other throttling behavior? We need a plan and ETA.

Attachments: charts_11_15.png (attachment stub), traces_sample_11_15.json (attachment stub)

Thanks,
Elena
Director of Platform
ClearBrooke AI
From: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@clearbrooke.ai>
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 22:30:12 -0000
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput collapse on our production traffic (charts attached)

Elena —

Thanks for the heads up and the artifacts. I’m escalating this internally and looping in Monica from Ops to triage immediately. Initial check: I’m not seeing a cluster-wide outage in our hosted fleet, so this looks like a per-customer throttling behavior (rate/quota/burst window) or a policy mismatch.

Immediate plan:
- Monica will pull the token bucket and burst-credit consumption history for your org.
- We’ll correlate the timestamps you provided with our rate limit logs and the routing layer.
- If this is a temporary quota squeeze, we can provision a short burst increase while we fix the root cause.

I’ll update within 30 minutes. Apologies for the disruption — we’ll treat this as high priority.

— Diego
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: Elena Torres <elena.torres@clearbrooke.ai>
Date: Sun, 15 Nov 2026 23:05:00 -0000
Subject: RE: Sudden throughput collapse on our production traffic (initial findings)

Diego / Kimberly / Elena —

Quick summary of what I’m seeing from the service logs and config diffs (attached):
1) Token-bucket burst window for ClearBrooke was configured with a short refill interval (t=1s) and a conservative burst credit cap. Their recent release created a sudden pattern of many medium-length streaming sessions which consumed burst credits faster than expected. The bucket exhausted and the request router started returning 429s under the current pacing regime.
2) There is a small misalignment between the shard-level quota (legacy) and the account-level burst policy. When the shard-level throttle tripped it caused cascading rejections instead of graceful shaping. I’ve attached a diff: burst-policy-diff-20261115.txt.
3) No GPU OOMs or model-side failures observed. This is policy-enforced backpressure at the ingress layer.

Remediation steps we recommend (short + medium term):
- Short term (minutes): apply a temporary burst-credit top-up for ClearBrooke (+150%) and increase the bucket cap. This requires exec approval for transient quota delta.
- Short-medium term (hours): harmonize shard vs account throttle rules for their tenant and push a patched policy that enables gradual shaping instead of hard 429 on burst exhaustion.
- Postmortem: run a rolling canary of the new policy for 24h and add a synthetic prompt set that mimics their streaming pattern to Optimize recommendations.

I’ve attached logs_snapshot_20261115.tar.gz with a filtered set of request ids for your triage. If we don’t do the temporary top-up we expect the customer demo to keep failing as they re-run sessions.

— Monica
Senior Site Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference
Attachment: logs_snapshot_20261115.tar.gz (1.2MB)
From: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
To: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 02:18:41 -0000
Subject: URGENT: Approval request — temporary burst-credit top-up for ClearBrooke (major demo impacted)

Marissa —

We have a P1 customer impact with ClearBrooke (see thread below). Monica’s triage indicates the root cause is a burst/quota policy configuration that exhausted token-bucket credits when the customer ramped a streaming-heavy release. The behavior is policy-induced backpressure (429s), not model or infra failures.

Customer impact: ongoing demo to enterprise prospect; estimated 30% request success drop during peak window (14:05–14:40 PST). If not mitigated, risk of churn / delayed renewal conversation.

Request (asks):
1) Immediate exec sign-off to grant a temporary burst-credit top-up of +150% for 4 hours to ClearBrooke while we push a patched policy. This is reversible and trackable.
2) Approval to provide a one-time service credit (worth ~2 days of usage) as a commercial gesture if the customer asks.

Estimated cost of top-up (4h): ~ $640 net (we will track and charge-back if required under their enterprise commit).

I recommend we approve the top-up now to restore their demo within minutes and then proceed with the policy harmonization patch. We’ll run a controlled canary and follow up with a full RCA.

Attaching: customer-impact-summary-11-16.pdf and the policy diff.

Please reply with APPROVE or DENY. If APPROVE, I’ll trigger the change and coordinate a post-change verification with ClearBrooke.

— Diego
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: diego_fernandez@redwood.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, monica_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 17:05:00 -0000
Subject: Re: URGENT: Approval request — temporary burst-credit top-up for ClearBrooke (major demo impacted)

Diego —

APPROVE the temporary +150% burst-credit top-up for 4 hours. Also approve the one-time commercial credit if ClearBrooke requests it; prioritize retention for this account.

Operational notes:
- Monica: execute the top-up now and confirm when the customer sees recovery (send me a brief status).
- Kimberly: please prep a short commercial note to offer if they escalate; keep value limited to the equivalent of 48 hours and tie acceptance to a commitment-to-review with their AM.

Keep me posted. If this repeats in the next 30 days propose a quota reforecast and pricing amendment.

— Marissa
VP, Customer Success & GTM, Redwood Inference
